text:
incident-bot: PAGER: Multi-GPU serving cluster showing repeated NCCL timeouts on tp4 pipeline jobs. Severity: P1. Affected region: us-west-2. Affected tenants: acme-prod (high), internal-canary. Symptoms: repeated GPU resets (Xid 79), container restarts, allreduce hangs. Runbook: https://go/runbooks/nccl-collective-hang

Ava (oncall): On it. Pulling logs, tagging folks. Allocating pager.

Rohit: I see repeating pattern in kernel logs on node gpu-node-23: "Xid 79: Choreographer detected GPU reset" then container OOMs. NCCL logs show repeated "NCCL WARN Allreduce op stalled: timeout". Raw snippet: ```
[2026-03-17T10:12:03Z] NCCL WARN 0 Allreduce timed out after 120s
[2026-03-17T10:12:03Z] process 0 aborted: cudaErrorLaunchTimeout
[2026-03-17T10:12:04Z] GPU 0 Xid 79 Reset
```

Jules: Tracing shows rendezvous leader flips between ranks 0 and 2 before hang. Likely network fabric jitter -> kernel resets -> nccl hangs. We should isolate node and fail traffic to redundant pool.

Marta: Customer impact: acme-prod error rate up to 8% for embeddings + generation since 10:11, median latency spiking 2x for affected requests. Canary failing 15% of runs. Estimating ~3k requests failed in last 10m.

Ava (oncall): Proposed immediate mitigations: 1) cordon/drain gpu-node-23 2) scale up fallback pool (single-gpu q8 model) and route acme-prod to it 3) restart nvidia driver / attempt module reload on node if we need it back quickly. Thoughts?

Priya: +1 to draining node. For customer continuity switch route first then drain to avoid in-flight failures. I can push traffic route update.

Rohit: Before reboot, try: ```sudo modprobe -r nvidia_uvm && sudo modprobe nvidia_uvm``` + restart container runtime on node. That has recovered similar Xid79s before. If that fails, do full node reboot.

Jules: I'll take the drain and route change. Doing staged failover: move acme-prod to dedicated-d2 pool, then move canary. Also enabling model-variant fallback for tp4 -> tp4-q8-single by routing policy.

Ava (oncall): Executing now. ps:kubectl cordon gpu-node-23 -> cordoned. kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data gpu-node-23 -> draining pods.

ops-bot: action:route-update acme-prod -> dedicated-d2 successful (req-weight 1.0)

Marta: Monitoring: error rate for acme-prod dropped to 1.2% after route flip, latency returning toward baseline. Canary still exhibits occasional timeouts (now 4%).

Rohit: Attempting driver module reload on gpu-node-23 now. Output: "nvidia_uvm removed" then "nvidia_uvm loaded". Restarting container runtime.

Ava (oncall): Pods are recreating on other nodes, some pods evicted. Seeing fewer NCCL WARNs in logs.

Jules: Post-failover checklist: leave node cordoned until we validate kernel/driver is stable for 30m. If module reload holds and NCCL logs quiet, we can uncordon.

Priya: Notifying SRE and account owner for ACME: @account-acme on-call notified with incident link and temporary mitigation note.

Marta: Customer impact update 10:32: acme-prod errors steady ~1%. Canary stable at ~2%. No new Xid79 events in last 3 minutes.

Ava (oncall): Agree to hold node cordoned. Schedule for deeper triage: collect full dmesg + nvml trace + core dumps if any. Ticketing: creating incident ticket and tagging infra/driver/telemetry teams.

Rohit: I'll grab nvml traces and GPU health metrics, push to /artifacts/incidents/5123456789. Also note driver version: 535.86.05, kernel 6.1. Repro rate low but correlated with heavy allreduce load (sequence length spikes).

Jules: Handing on-call to Jules (night shift) at 11:00 PST for monitoring & remediation follow-up. Ava will brief postmortem owners. :thumbsup:

Ava (oncall): Handoff ack. Please keep escalation channel open and update this thread with any driver reoccurrence. We'll tag for postmortem and RCA: suspected fabric + driver interaction under heavy TP4 allreduce backpressure.

incident-bot: Incident updated: status=stabilized, mitigation=traffic-failover+driver-reload, impacted=acme-prod, severity=P1->P2 (monitoring). Link: https://go/incidents/5123456789

Marta: Logged customer communications draft; will send TOU update after sign-off.

Priya: I'll coordinate with account to schedule a follow-up call if they request.

ops-bot: reminder: collect logs (dmesg, nvml, container logs) before uncordon.

Jules: Leaving monitoring dashboards on. If no new Xid79 within 30m, plan to uncordon tomorrow 02:00 UTC and run staged rejoin with low-traffic canary.

Ava (oncall): Closing active paging loop; keeping incident open for postmortem and follow-up actions. Great job team. :heart:
